version.changelog:
Initial release of WechatSync.

- Publish and sync Markdown/HTML articles to 27+ platforms (including Zhihu, Juejin, CSDN, Bilibili, WeChat, WordPress, and more) via CLI.
- Supports multi-platform publishing, content distribution, and draft sync.
- Check login status for all or specific platforms.
- Extract articles from browser pages and save to file.
- Supports custom titles, cover images, and preview mode.
- Images auto-uploaded to target platform CDN and articles sync as drafts for review.

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: wechatsync
Version: 1.0.0

The wechatsync skill is a legitimate tool designed for multi-platform article distribution and content synchronization across various Chinese tech and social media platforms. It acts as a wrapper for the @wechatsync/cli npm package, requiring a user-provided WECHATSYNC_TOKEN for authentication. The instructions in SKILL.md are consistent with the tool's stated purpose, and no indicators of data exfiltration, malicious execution, or harmful prompt injection were found.

llm.summary: The skill's instructions ask you to install an unvetted npm CLI and a Chrome extension and to set a token that grants access to your browser/session data, but the skill metadata declares no credentials or installs — those mismatches and the external install surface are concerning.

dimensions.detail: The description says this is a CLI-based cross-posting tool, which plausibly needs a CLI and browser integration to access logged-in sessions. However the skill metadata declares no required env vars, binaries, or install steps, while SKILL.md instructs installing an npm package (@wechatsync/cli) and a Chrome extension and setting WECHATSYNC_TOKEN. The declared manifest therefore does not match the runtime requirements in SKILL.md.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions tell the user/agent to install a browser extension, enable an opaque "MCP Connection" and obtain a token, log into many platforms in the browser, and use an 'extract from current browser page' feature. Those steps require access to browser tabs, cookies, and possibly account sessions — broader access than the skill manifest states and potentially capable of reading or transmitting unrelated sensitive data.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no formal install spec in the manifest, but SKILL.md instructs running `npm install -g @wechatsync/cli` and installing an extension from https://www.wechatsync.com/#install. Both the npm package and the website/extension are external/unvetted in this bundle. Installing third-party npm packages and browser extensions can execute arbitrary code and access sensitive browser data; the SKILL.md does not provide source/repo links or integrity information.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The manifest lists no required environment variables, yet SKILL.md requires setting WECHATSYNC_TOKEN (sensitive). The token likely grants the CLI/extension access to the browser/session. The skill also relies on the user being logged into many external platforms in the browser, which further multiplies sensitive access. These credentials/access requests are not declared in the metadata and are broad relative to the manifest.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill itself is instruction-only and not marked always:true; however it instructs installing a browser extension and creating a token—that extension (outside the agent) would have persistent presence in the user's browser. Autonomous model invocation is enabled by default (normal), and combined with an externally persistent extension/token this increases potential blast radius if the external components are compromised.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill is suspicious because its runtime steps require installing and trusting external software (an npm package and a Chrome extension) and setting a WECHATSYNC_TOKEN that can give access to your browser sessions, but the skill metadata doesn't declare those requirements. Before installing or using it: 1) verify the npm package and extension source — find the package/extension repository and inspect its code and permissions; 2) check the extension's Chrome store page and permissions (what host data it can read); 3) avoid using your primary accounts — test with disposable/test accounts first; 4) do not export or paste sensitive tokens into shared environments; 5) prefer tools whose manifests declare required env vars and whose code is auditable; 6) if you must use it, run the CLI and extension in an isolated environment (VM) and review network traffic to understand what is transmitted. If you cannot verify the origin and code of the CLI/extension, treat it as high-risk and avoid installing it on production or personal machines.
